measurement_note: The op-level forward launches three device kernels (_scan_main + _expand_main + main_mix_aic) and the op-level msprof capture fails for three of four tune shapes on this toolchain; the target kernel is therefore profiled standalone (schedule tables materialised on device by the sibling scheduler before the timed region, then the GEMM launched warmup+iters times). Metric is msprof-native Task Duration(us) + the GM/L2 `GM Read + Write` roofline Ratio.
wrapper_pairing_required: The wrapper passes block_m/block_n/block_k/num_stages EXPLICITLY to both factories, so flipping the perf_opt import alone is NOT sufficient: MoeGroupedGemmNopadKernel.default_config must return dict(TUNED_DEFAULT_CONFIG) (import it from .moe_grouped_gemm_nopad_kernel.perf_opt._moe_grouped_gemm_kernel). block_m is also the shared constant with the scheduler (max_tiles = numel // block_m + E), so the wrapper's max_tiles must be recomputed from the tuned block_m (it already is: _max_tiles uses self.config['block_m']). Wrapper files are NOT modified by Stage 4.

scheduler_kernel.reason: The scheduler is two Vector kernels over E-sized int32 tables (E=256 -> ~3 KB of traffic). Measured standalone with msprof op (this task, E=256/numel=32768/block_m=128): _scan_main 10.10 us + _expand_main 13.80 us ~= 24 us per forward, i.e. 0.15%-0.4% of the GEMM target kernel (5.7-15.9 ms). It is not part of the benchmark's Roofline target (msprof_kernel_name = main_mix_aic) and therefore carries no benchmark workload of its own. Shipped unchanged (byte-identical logic + mode self-pinning) so the perf_opt pair adopts atomically; regression `perf_opt/_tile_scheduler_kernel.py --level all` passes.
